title: Progressive cost circuit-breaker and GPU family adjudicator for spot/on-demand routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a tenant-aware, progressive cost 'circuit-breaker' that enforces per-tenant budget caps and drives region/tier/GPU-family routing decisions with graceful degradation to cheaper model variants.

Background: Current routing favors capacity-first heuristics and separate spot/on-demand policies. We need a unified controller that enforces soft and hard spend limits, reduces SLO surprises during surge/spot-eviction windows, and chooses GPU family + model-variant combos that meet latency and quality constraints while respecting tenant budgets.

Proposal summary:
1) Cost Circuit: per-tenant windowed spend counters with three modes: open (normal routing), throttled (prefer cheaper variants / lower-tier regions / mixed GPU families), and tripped (hard limit => reject or queue with a clear error). Transitions are probabilistic and rate-limited to avoid oscillation.
2) GPU Family Adjudicator: scoring function that ranks available device families per-request using: estimated per-token cost, eviction risk score (from spot telemetry), predicted latency delta, and model-variant quality delta. We treat GPU family as a first-class routing dimension (not only region).
3) Model Variant Ladder: pre-authorize variants (full-fp, quantized-ptq, 4-bit, distilled) with known quality regressions and cost multipliers. The circuit can step traffic down the ladder for throttled tenants.
4) Soft vs Hard caps: soft caps trigger preference shifts (probabilistic reroutes), hard caps trigger immediate enforcement (retries into queue or RFC-style 402-like error).
5) Safety nets: eviction-aware headroom reserve for in-flight requests; a short 'graceful-fallback' window to complete existing streams on a higher-cost instance where feasible.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Probabilistic throttling reduces hard-switched outages but complicates billing predictability. We favour a hybrid: deterministic for hard caps, probabilistic for soft.
- Preferring lower-cost regions will add cross-region network egress for some tenants; we include egress cost in the adjudicator score and make this opt-in via tenant setting.
- GPU family scoring uses historical latency distributions; cold-starts for new families will fall back to conservative bias (prefer well-known families).

API/Config surface:
- New tenant config: {"daily_budget_usd", "soft_threshold_pct", "hard_threshold_pct", "prefer_low_egress": true/false, "variant_ladder": [variant_ids], "gpu_family_preferences": []} (stored in Tenant Config service).
- Runtime: routing decision logs will emit adjudicator_reason and score breakdown for observability and billing reconciliation.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end simulation shows per-tenant spend stays within +/-5% of configured hard cap under synthetic surge scenarios.
- No SLO regression (>1% increase in p99 latency) for P0 tenants when running throttled policy compared to baseline.
- Circuit transitions and model-variant degradations are visible in Console with per-tenant timeline and replay logs.

Monitoring & metrics:
- per-tenant: windowed_spend_usd, soft_hits, hard_trips, routed_variant_id, routed_gpu_family, adjudicator_score_components.
- system: total_re-routes_per_min, percent_requests_routed_to_spot, percent_requests_degraded_to_quantized, eviction_recovery_success_rate.

Rollout plan:
1) Integration tests + load simulation in staging (2 weeks).
2) Canary: enable soft-mode for internal tenants and 3 pilot customers; collect metrics for 1 week.
3) Gradual expansion with feature-flag gating and kill-switch.

Backwards compatibility: default tenant config is permissive (no implicit hard caps). All logic is behind feature flag 'cost_circuit_v2' per-tenant.

Docs & artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Cost+Circuit+v2 ; prototype notebook: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/s/RC-proto-circuit-v2 ; routing-sim repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-sim/pull/231

Notes: Implementation touches tenant-config, routing-planner, runtime-adjudicator, console telemetry pipeline, billing reconciliation. Expect collaboration with billing and console teams for validation.
